cases.case_title: TRG Financial Academy and fake Axis Bank Securities investment fraud
cases.court_or_authority: Andhra Pradesh High Court at Amaravati
cases.case_number: Criminal Petition No.6609/2025; Crime No.63/2025, Mandapeta Town Police Station
cases.platform_primary: WhatsApp / purported Axis Bank Securities app
cases.impersonated_identity_detail: TRG Financial Academy and a purported SEBI-registered Axis Bank Securities investment application
cases.initial_contact_summary: A 27-year-old UPSC aspirant was introduced to alleged fraudsters through a WhatsApp group called TRG Financial Academy offering investment classes.
cases.pretext_summary: The group promoted a purported Axis Bank Securities application that appeared legitimate/SEBI-registered, then demanded investment, IPO and later tax/error/frozen-account payments.
cases.other_psychological_mechanism: Legitimacy borrowing from a known financial brand and SEBI, escalating sunk-cost pressure and withdrawal/account-freeze barriers.
cases.requested_action: Install/use the purported investment app and make repeated investment, IPO, tax and account-unfreeze payments.
cases.victim_action: The complainant made repeated payments beginning with INR 3.5 million and ultimately paid approximately INR 6.2 million.
cases.other_evidence: Bank-account freeze and investigation of accounts used to route victim funds.
cases.attribution_target: Ahsan Khan's beneficiary-account role and the unresolved TRG/app operators.
cases.attribution_limitations: The petitioner was not identified as a victim-facing operator. The order records that his account was used for approximately INR 3.5 million and his defence that he shared the account for promised trading returns before learning of the fraud.
cases.alternative_explanation: Ahsan Khan argued that he was an indirect victim who provided his bank account for trading in exchange for promised monthly payments/profits and received only INR 10,000.
cases.primary_evidentiary_gap: Authenticated WhatsApp/app/device records connecting the TRG Financial Academy and fake investment application to identified operators and showing the petitioner's knowledge or coordination.
cases.legal_provisions: BNS Section 318(4); Information Technology Act Section 66-D
cases.disposition: Andhra Pradesh High Court granted Ahsan Khan bail on 16 July 2025 while investigation was incomplete and charge sheet had not yet been filed.
cases.case_summary: A 27-year-old UPSC aspirant in Mandapeta joined a WhatsApp group called TRG Financial Academy, which offered financial-investment classes and promoted a purported Axis Bank Securities app represented as legitimate and SEBI-linked. Beginning in December 2024, she made a large initial investment and additional IPO, tax and account-correction payments. Her account was later shown as frozen on a pretext of incorrect bank details and further payments were demanded, bringing the alleged total to about INR 62 lakh. The bail record says Ahsan Khan provided an account used to route approximately INR 35 lakh; he claimed he had shared the account for trading in return for promised profits and was himself an indirect victim. The case adds a new state and a clean example of strong financial-endpoint evidence without victim-facing identity resolution.
cases.research_notes: Incident start date is supported by the order's statement that investment began on 23 December 2024. Incident end date is left blank because the order does not provide a complete day-level end date. Amount normalized to INR 6.2 million from the source's OCR-distorted but textually clear Rs.62,00,000 figure.

actors.conduct_assessed: Answering the customer-care call, impersonating Prestige support and directing the victim into the fraudulent link/application flow.

actors.conduct_assessed: Calling the victim with a reward-points pretext and sending the phishing link used to collect card information.

actors.conduct_assessed: Operating email/phone identities and banking channels used to send recruitment material and receive payments.

actors.conduct_assessed: Sending replacement-charge demands while impersonating boAt/Imagine Marketing and directing customers to UPI payments.

actors.conduct_assessed: Operating WhatsApp/Telegram/social-media identities that used the plaintiff's name/image and represented investment advice as genuine.

actors.function_assignment_basis: no paper-specific evidence assigning either primary function

actors.conduct_assessed: Using senior-personnel names/photos and WhatsApp groups to solicit investments under the ChrysCapital identity.

actors.conduct_assessed: Operating the fake investment registration/website/payment layer used to convert impersonation into financial transfers.

actors.conduct_assessed: Publishing AI/deepfake videos using Warikoo's face and voice and directing viewers to investment groups.

actors.conduct_assessed: Sending the KYC SMS/link that induced the senior citizen to click a purported verification flow.

sources.claim_scope: A Chandigarh consumer appeal examined an INR 49,997 internet-banking transaction after the complainant clicked a purported eKYC link. The commission characterized the allegations as involving phishing/impersonation but found no proven bank-system failure.
sources.notes: Final/adjudicatory material; underlying criminal guilt is not inferred beyond the source's procedural findings.

sources.title: Rishabh Gehlot v. State (NCT of Delhi), 13 April 2026
sources.claim_scope: A Delhi High Court bail order describes a long-running deception using the persona 'Shaurya' and multiple shifting pretexts, including government jobs, tenders, investments and personal emergencies. The prosecution relied on WhatsApp chats, audio recordings and bank statements, while disputing which communications involved the bail applicant.
sources.notes: Bail/interim-stage material; allegations and prima facie observations are not treated as final findings.

sources.title: A.A. Abdulla v. Union of India, 28 March 2025
sources.claim_scope: The Kerala High Court recorded a digital-arrest style fraud in which a FedEx narcotics pretext escalated to Mumbai Cyber Crime impersonation and induced a 75-year-old victim to transfer INR 10,440,111. The judgment transferred the investigation to the CBI because the perpetrators and transactions appeared spread across multiple states.
sources.notes: Final/adjudicatory material; underlying criminal guilt is not inferred beyond the source's procedural findings.

sources.title: Anshu Yadav v. State of Haryana, 17 July 2026
sources.claim_scope: A Punjab and Haryana High Court bail order records a WhatsApp family-impersonation fraud in which a caller posed as the complainant's relative abroad and used a medical-emergency pretext to induce transfers of about INR 799,000. Police traced one beneficiary account to the petitioner, who claimed his account and ATM had been misused by another person.
sources.notes: Bail/interim-stage material; allegations and prima facie observations are not treated as final findings.

sources.title: State Bank of India v. G. Natrajan, 9 July 2026
sources.publisher_or_authority: Delhi State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
sources.court_or_body: Delhi State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
sources.claim_scope: A Delhi consumer appeal records a KYC smishing incident in which a senior citizen clicked a verification link and then suffered INR 45,000 in unauthorized transactions. The record included the original SMS and banking complaint documents.
sources.notes: Final/adjudicatory material; underlying criminal guilt is not inferred beyond the source's procedural findings.

sources.title: State Bank of India v. Prabhu Lal, 28 April 2026
sources.publisher_or_authority: Madhya Pradesh State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
sources.court_or_body: Madhya Pradesh State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
sources.claim_scope: A Madhya Pradesh consumer appeal documents a classic vishing case in which a caller impersonating the bank's main branch used ATM blocking/Aadhaar-linking as a pretext to obtain card details, followed by eight online purchases. The commission ultimately attributed contributory negligence to the complainant in the banking-liability dispute.
sources.notes: Final/adjudicatory material; underlying criminal guilt is not inferred beyond the source's procedural findings.

sources.title: ChrysCapital Advisors LLP v. Raj Lal Kumari & Ors., 29 May 2024
sources.claim_scope: Interim order describing WhatsApp groups, impersonated senior personnel, fake registration documents, the fraudulent ChrysCapital-branded website, victim complaints and platform/telecom disclosure directions.
sources.notes: Independent procedural-stage source within the same civil litigation; useful for contemporaneous modus-operandi detail and provider-disclosure directions.

sources.title: Freeman Anosike Aluma v. CBI, 16 October 2018
sources.court_or_body: Special Judge-07 (Central), Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi
sources.claim_scope: Appellate reconstruction of 2008 HDFC phishing, bank/login/IP/telecom evidence, witness-based financial linkage, Section 65-B material, CERT-In analysis and omitted GEQD phone/SIM report; conviction set aside and matter remanded.
sources.notes: Judicial record accessed through Indian Kanoon mirror; underlying source is a court judgment.

sources.title: M/s Canara Bank & 2 Ors. v. Vijayakumaran Raghavan, 4 December 2019
sources.claim_scope: Appellate consumer decision describing hacked/imitated email instructions, overseas transfers of USD 86,500 and bank verification failures; confirms most substantive relief while modifying compensation.
sources.notes: Formal statutory adjudicatory material coded T1; criminal authorship of the unknown email operator was not adjudicated.

sources.title: Vijayakumaran Raghavan v. Chairman and MD, Canara Bank, 28 September 2015
sources.publisher_or_authority: Kerala State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
sources.court_or_body: Kerala State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
sources.claim_scope: Original consumer adjudication detailing email compromise warning, disputed transfer instructions, overseas transfers, bank records and FIR-related material.
sources.notes: Supporting T1 adjudicatory source; amounts vary by small transcription inconsistencies across the source and appeal, so the Atlas uses the repeatedly stated INR 48,25,671 figure.

sources.title: State Bank of India v. Pallabh Bhowmick & 4 Ors., 13 September 2024
sources.claim_scope: Appellate judgment on unauthorized Louis Philippe refund-app transactions; identifies Papendra Kumar in the record, details beneficiary transfers, OTP logs and retailer data-breach correspondence.
sources.notes: Judgment resolves bank/customer liability; it is not a criminal conviction of the identified respondent.

sources.title: State Bank of India v. Kodudhala Joji Reddy (Deceased) & Anr., 17 November 2025
sources.claim_scope: Revision decision reconstructing 2015 SBI debit-card verification vishing against senior-citizen account holders and unexplained withdrawals despite a PIN change; bank revision dismissed.
sources.notes: Adjudicates consumer liability and system gaps, not identity of the untraced caller or cash-out actor.

sources.title: Rajesh Kumar Kashyap v. Union Territory of J&K, 30 July 2021
sources.publisher_or_authority: High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh
sources.claim_scope: Bail order reconstructing Facebook/WhatsApp Christina George advance-fee fraud, fake customs/embassy personas, INR 88,58,883 transfers, false identity documents and alleged downstream/organising roles.
sources.notes: Order contains inconsistent FIR references in different paragraphs; Atlas records the bail application number and does not silently reconcile the FIR number.

sources.title: Vivek Keshavan v. Central Bureau of Investigation, 20 February 2024
sources.claim_scope: Charge-stage review of alleged PMO Principal Secretary impersonation seeking vehicle/accommodation/protocol facilities; discusses e-KYC, subscriber records, CDRs, WhatsApp messages and witness evidence.
sources.notes: High Court dismissed challenge to charge-stage orders; material is prima facie and guilt remained for trial.

sources.title: Divya Pandey v. State of Bihar, 5 March 2025
sources.case_number: CR. MISC. No.72271 of 2024; Khagaria (Cyber) P.S. Case No.20/2023
sources.claim_scope: Bail order describing Alliance Solution investment pretext, phone/WhatsApp/email/website communications, forged agreements and offices, INR 53.5 lakh transfers, initial payouts and downstream account investigation.
sources.notes: Petitioner-specific account figures differ within the bail submissions; these are preserved as limitations rather than harmonized into a definitive amount.

sources.title: Muliyasiya Anil Sarman v. State (U.T. of A & N Islands), 5 February 2026
sources.claim_scope: Bail order describing phone-based digital arrest, INR 1 crore transferred to three accounts, one apprehended beneficiary account holder and prosecution's mastermind allegation based on a co-accused statement.
sources.notes: High Court expressly noted apparent absence of independent material beyond the co-accused statement linking petitioner and granted bail.

sources.title: Ritu Gupta v. State (NCT of Delhi), 16 March 2026
sources.claim_scope: Bail order reconstructing terrorism-pretext digital arrest of an elderly couple, secrecy/hourly reporting, INR 94.5 lakh transfers and the applicant's INR 40 lakh account receipt plus competing account/SIM-misuse defence.
sources.notes: Previously logged as CAND-0031 pending under an earlier stopping rule; Wave 1A promotes that same candidate rather than adding a duplicate screening entry.

sources.title: Ahsan Khan v. State of Andhra Pradesh, 16 July 2025
sources.claim_scope: Bail order describing TRG Financial Academy WhatsApp investment classes, a purported Axis Bank Securities app, escalating payments totalling about INR 62 lakh and use of the petitioner's account for approximately INR 35 lakh.
sources.notes: Investigation incomplete and charge sheet not filed at time of bail; petitioner described himself as an indirect victim who shared his account for promised trading returns.
